summary: This benchmark evaluates whether allowing unedited native coordinates to evolve while preserving only donor displacement recovers performance lost during multi-block activation transplants between Qwen2.5 models. The empirical results show that the native-relative hold yields 332/512 complete carry groups compared to 333/512 for an absolute hold and 358/512 for a one-shot splice, demonstrating that the transplant penalty persists despite moving references. The methodology is mathematically well-specified with negative controls and paired confidence intervals, though the write-up is extremely compact and relies on prior unstated context.
strengths: Rigorous experimental design featuring explicit control arms, including an orthogonal projection control (0/512) and native preservation verification (512/512).
Precise mathematical formulation of the native-relative displacement update rule and coordinate projection.
Comprehensive reporting of statistical uncertainty using paired 95% confidence intervals (-1.76 to +1.56 percentage points between relative and absolute holds).
Thorough documentation of runtime parameters, software dependency versions, peak memory allocations, and hardware execution environment.
weaknesses: Highly compressed exposition (536 words) that assumes familiarity with predecessor protocols without fully defining the four-variant carry panel task in the article text.
Evaluation is narrow, focusing exclusively on two assignment positions within a single arithmetic carry dataset without probing general model degradation or language coherence elsewhere.
Categorized under the text_only review track without a bundled repository package in the submission metadata, requiring reliance on external URLs for code verification.
suggestions: Include a concise self-contained description and example of the 512 four-variant arithmetic group prompt template and qualification criteria.
Expand evaluation to test whether seven-block holds cause out-of-distribution perplexity degradation or token regression on unrelated standard language tasks.

claims.text: The donor is frozen BF16 Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (0396a761, width 3,584, read after block six).
The original seven axes were fitted in Qwen2.5-14B (97e1e763, width 5,120, block ten).
The frozen BF16 recipient is Qwen2.5-32B (1818d358, width 5,120, 64 blocks).

Holding only the donor's initial displacement while allowing the unedited reference to evolve gave 332 complete carry groups out of 512. Freezing the seven absolute values gave 333, and a single early splice gave 358.
